_help: Triage settings for the test dashboard (reports/index.html). Shared through git: edit, commit, push.
modules: the app's areas, who owns each, and areas deliberately not tested (shown as coverage gaps or exclusions).
tests: module and severity per test ID. A [P0]/[P1] tag in the test title also sets the severity. Default P2.
issues: per error signature: owner, ticket link, known issue. The dashboard's Assign / Ticket / Mark as known buttons
edit these in your browser; 'Download triage.json' then gives you this file with your changes, to replace it here.
ticket.newIssueUrl: where 'Create ticket' opens a pre-filled issue (GitHub style ?title=&body=).
knownApi: API problems that are understood and not a test failure; matched against the call's endpoint or URL. Shown grey, not red.

quarantine: tests whose failures do not count towards the verdict until a date: [{ test, reason, owner, until: 'YYYY-MM-DD', ticket, added }]. After 'until' the failure counts again and the verdict says the quarantine expired. The dashboard's Quarantine button adds entries (then Download triage.json).

categoryRules: your own rules for failure categories, checked before the built-in ones: [{ match: 'regular expression on the error message', category: 'product' | 'test' | 'environment' | 'infrastructure' | 'review', why: 'shown as the reason' }]. issues.<signature>.category overrides one failure by hand.

Login / Account.excluded: Not tested on purpose: tests must not log in to the live Wikipedia site

Editing.excluded: Not tested on purpose: tests must never edit the live Wikipedia site

knownApi.reason: The dev build fetches its analytics settings from Wikimedia's test (beta) servers, which refuse it (403). Not caused by the tests; the prod build uses meta.wikimedia.org.
